method.name: milp_production_inventory_backlog
steps: Define integer production variables for each product (I,II,III) in each quarter (Q1-Q4), non-negative inventory variables, and non-negative backlog variables.
Zero production for product I in Q2.
Inventory balance: inv[p,q] = inv[p,q-1] + prod[p,q] - demand[p,q] + backlog[p,q-1] - backlog[p,q]. Initial inv at Q1 start = 0.

Backlog penalty accumulated: each unit of backlog at end of quarter q has been delayed q quarters, so total backlog delay cost = 20*(1*bl[I,Q1]+2*bl[I,Q2]+3*bl[I,Q3]+4*bl[I,Q4]) + same pattern for II + 10*(1*bl[III,Q1]+...+4*bl[III,Q4]).
Final inventory >= 150 for each product at end of Q4.
Use HiGHS high-level API (addVariable/addConstr/getSolution) to solve as MILP with integer production variables.

method.name: milp_time_indexed_aggregate_cost
steps: Use aggregate cost approach: define effective backlog cost rate per quarter that accumulates delay penalty.
Production variables for each product in each quarter, non-negative integer.
Inventory balance per product per quarter: ending_inv = beginning_inv + production - demand. If ending_inv < 0, treat absolute value as backlog.
Use indicator constraints or SOS to separate positive inventory (holding) from negative inventory (backlog).
Quarter-specific backlog penalty rates: Q1 delay=20/10 per unit, Q2 delay=40/20, Q3 delay=60/30, Q4 delay=80/40 for I,II/III.
Holding cost 5 per unit per quarter on positive inventory only.
HiGHS MILP with integer production variables.
